name: Tettra
tagline: Internal wiki and knowledge workflows integrated with team chat

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Scaling
tiers.limits: 10-user minimum; unlimited storage and version history; AI, Slack, Google Workspace, analytics, and API access.
tiers.notes: Displayed annual rate; the live page advertises monthly billing but did not expose its exact toggled amount.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom price; SSO and SCIM included; discounted rates beyond 250 licenses.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (20% off advertised); exact monthly amount was not independently exposed; 30-day trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Scaling has a 10-user minimum; SAML SSO, SCIM, and group permissions are paid add-ons on Scaling but included in Enterprise.

verdictSummary: The visible knowledge management loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Tettra earns its keep through collaboration, integrations, polish, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a single-user knowledge management workspace with projects, tasks, statuses, filters, recurring items, and JSON export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Tettra: Teams pay because shared state, notifications, permissions, and migrations are harder than the visible board or list.
ongoingBurden: Maintain notifications, recurring-date logic, importers, permissions, backups, and collaboration conflict handling.

priorArt.name: Vikunja
priorArt.desc: Open-source task manager with lists, boards, and collaboration.

rejectedAlternatives.name: AppFlowy
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It stores team knowledge, but the free self-hosted collaboration tier is one seat plus guests

rejectedAlternatives.name: Docmost
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A strong wiki with search, but no verification or chat-native answer workflow

rejectedAlternatives.name: Outline
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A polished wiki, but self-hosting is paid and it lacks Tettra's chat-native knowledge workflow

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Tettra is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Tettra, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a single-user knowledge management workspace with projects, tasks, statuses, filters, recurring items, and JSON export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: real-time multiplayer; enterprise permissions; large integration catalog.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
